anatomy.lede: The gulper eel has stripped its body down to a huge, loosely hinged mouth and a long, whip-thin tail, with very little in between.

hotspots.label: Snout
hotspots.text: Its tiny eyes sit close to the tip of the snout, far from the hinge of the enormous jaws.

hotspots.label: Lower jaw
hotspots.text: The jaws extend far back along the body, enlarging the mouth enormously. They carry several rows of small teeth.

hotspots.label: Expandable mouth
hotspots.text: The mouth cavity is greatly distensible, opening like a net to take in prey together with a large volume of water.

hotspots.label: Whip-like tail
hotspots.text: The body tapers into a very long, thin tail with no tail fin. In intact specimens it ends in an expanded light-producing organ.

senses.lede: Its senses have barely been studied, but its anatomy offers clues — especially in mature males.

senses.name: Smell
senses.text: At maturity males' smell organs enlarge while their jaws and teeth degenerate, suggesting that finding a mate by scent becomes their main task.

senses.name: Lateral line
senses.text: Instead of a line of pores along its sides, its lateral line — the system fishes use to sense water movement — is made of groups of raised tubules.

senses.name: Sight
senses.text: Its eyes are tiny; how much it relies on them in the near-darkness where it lives is not known.

body.lede: Much of the usual fish anatomy is missing: the gulper eel has no scales, no tail fin and no fin spines.

systems.title: Mouth as a scoop
systems.text: Prey is taken in along with water, which is then pushed out through the gill openings.

systems.title: A pared-down body
systems.text: It lacks scales, a tail fin and dorsal or anal fin spines, and its body is long and eel-like behind the head.

mind.lede: Almost everything known about its behaviour comes from a few chance encounters with underwater cameras.

studies.title: The black balloon
studies.text: Near a mile down off Hawaiʻi, a remotely operated vehicle filmed a young gulper eel inflating its mouth like a balloon, then deflating it and swimming off.

studies.title: A threat response?
studies.text: After seeing a gulper eel inflate in the Gulf of Mexico, some researchers suggested the display happens when the fish feels threatened.

studies.title: Mapping where it lives
studies.text: Modelling of museum records predicted a near-worldwide range, with gaps such as the Southern Ocean and Bering Sea. The gulper eel is not known to migrate up and down the water column each day.

life.lede: Its life cycle is pieced together from preserved specimens and from what is known of related eels.

stages.name: Egg
stages.text: Eggs are released into the open water and drift as plankton.

stages.name: Leptocephalus larva
stages.text: Eggs hatch into leptocephalus larvae, the drifting larval form of eels, which live in the plankton.

stages.name: Adult
stages.text: At maturity males change shape: their smell organs grow while their teeth and jaws shrink. Females remain relatively unchanged.

stages.name: Spawning
stages.text: Degenerative changes in both sexes suggest gulper eels may spawn only once and then die.
